turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My coworker just lost her dad and we usually swap gifts.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Give me a second, my brother needs help with something. Stay quiet until I'm back.

turns.speaker: moshi

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Theo, do you want the window seat or the aisle?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Window, if that's okay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So how much English did people speak in Japan?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: In Tokyo, quite a bit at hotels and stations. Outside the city, way less.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Did you manage with your Japanese?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Barely. I could say thank you, excuse me and where's the toilet. That covered a lot.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should I bother learning more before I go?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Yes, even a few more phrases. People lit up when I tried.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay. Which phrase was the most useful?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Excuse me. Sumimasen. You use it for everything.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Alright, I'm back with you.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sure thing. So what feels right for her this year?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A card. And maybe offer to take her to lunch.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's thoughtful. Lunch gives her company without pressure.
